subject: Fed raises rates for first time in three years
preview_text: The Fed lifts its target range to 3.75%-4.00% as inflation stays elevated; another increase may follow this year.
description: The September 17, 2026 morning edition of The Rally Brief from Rally Point News Desk.
content_html:
The Rally Brief · September 17, 2026

The morning picture

The Federal Reserve has shifted back toward tighter monetary policy. On Wednesday, the FOMC unanimously raised the federal-funds target range by a quarter point to 3.75%-4.00%, its first rate increase in more than three years. The Fed says economic activity remains solid but inflation is still elevated.

The decision matters immediately for borrowing costs and signals that policymakers are prepared to keep pressure on inflation even as geopolitical uncertainty remains high. Fed projections indicate another increase could follow before year-end.

The Fed turns toward tightening

The Federal Reserve's own statement says domestic spending has remained resilient, productivity growth is strong and unemployment has changed little. Inflation, however, remains above the central bank's goal. The committee said the increase is intended to support a more timely return to 2% inflation.

Federal Reserve: September 16 FOMC statement →

Reuters reports that policymakers' latest projections point to one additional rate increase this year. Major U.S. banks subsequently raised their prime lending rates, meaning the policy shift can flow through to variable-rate borrowing for households and businesses.

Reuters: Fed projections and the path ahead →

Why inflation is back at the center

Chair Kevin Warsh said the economy has strengthened but inflation remains the central problem. The rate decision arrives as high energy costs and geopolitical disruptions add another layer of price pressure. That makes the Fed story part of a larger economic picture Rally Point has been tracking rather than an isolated policy move.
